newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatargas borrows $570 mln for gas export project.
newsitem.headline: Qatargas borrows $570 mln for gas export project.

text.p: Qatar said on Saturday it had signed a 12-year $570 million loan with four foreign banks to cover the building cost of one of its three major gas export projects.

"We signed the loan for building upstream facilities for Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas) on December 12, although the project has already gone on stream (in September)," Qatargas vice-chairman Faisal al-Suweidi told Reuters.
Qatargas, the first of the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state's three multi-billion-dollar projects, originally sought the loan in 1994.
But industry sources said the deal was delayed because of differences between the participating European banks, one of which eventually pulled out of the syndication.
The loan was arranged by France's Credit Lyonnais and Societe Generale, Britain's Barclays Plc and Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank. Five other banks have underwritten the facility.

The loan, a mix of buyers' credit and commercial debt, was signed in London, Al-Suweidi said. It will cover around 70 percent of the cost of drilling wells, building offshore platforms and piping gas onshore to a liquefaction plant.
Qatargas officials said shareholders shared the cost during the construction stage. "Now, they will be able to recover the money from the loan," an official said.
Qatargas is 65 percent owned by the Qatar government, 10 percent each by U.S. Mobil Corp and France's Total and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Mitsui and Marubeni corporations.
It is set to start shipping LNG to Japan later this week.

The loan deal signed this month was the second financing arrangement sought by Qatargas to execute the project designed to supply six million tonnes a year of LNG to Japan for 25 years from January 1997.

The first loan of $2 billion for constructing downstream facilities -- a liquefaction plant and storage tanks -- was arranged by Japanese banks, led by Export and Import (EXIM) Bank of Japan and Bank of Tokyo in mid-1995.
Like the first loan this facility spans over 12 years, including a grace period of two years, and carries a "very attractive rate", a Qatar General Petroleum Corp official said.
Qatar's other gas export projects are Ras Laffan LNG Company and Qatar-Enron LNG Marketing Company.
